--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -247,30 +247,31 @@
-    origlen = len(v)
-    v = v.lstrip(alphabet[0:1])
-    nzeros = origlen - len(v)
-
-    info = None
-    if isinstance(v, bytes) and type(alphabet) is bytes:
-        cache = _DECODE_INFO_AF if autofix else _DECODE_INFO
-        info = cache.get(alphabet)
-        if info is None and len(alphabet) < 255:
-            base = len(alphabet)
-            pv = _pair_values(base)
-            b2 = base * base
-            info = (_get_base58_translate_table(alphabet, bool(autofix)),
-                    b2 * b2, [x * b2 for x in pv], pv)
-            cache[alphabet] = info
-    if info is not None:
-        table, b4, p2, pv = info
-        digits = v.translate(table)
-        if b'\xff' not in digits:
-            digits = _ZPAD8[len(digits) & 7] + digits
-            acc = 0
-            it = iter(memoryview(digits).cast('H'))
-            for p, q, r, s in zip(it, it, it, it):
-                acc = (acc * b4 + (p2[p] + pv[q])) * b4 + (p2[r] + pv[s])
-        else:
-            acc = b58decode_int(v, alphabet=alphabet, autofix=autofix)
-    else:
-        acc = b58decode_int(v, alphabet=alphabet, autofix=autofix)
-
-    return acc.to_bytes(nzeros + (acc.bit_length() + 7) // 8, 'big')
+    origlen = len(v)
+    info = None
+    if type(alphabet) is bytes and isinstance(v, bytes):
+        info = (_DECODE_INFO_AF if autofix else _DECODE_INFO).get(alphabet)
+        if info is None and len(alphabet) < 255:
+            base = len(alphabet)
+            pv = _pair_values(base)
+            b2 = base * base
+            b4 = b2 * b2
+            b6 = b4 * b2
+            info = (_get_base58_translate_table(alphabet, bool(autofix)),
+                    b4 * b4, [x * b6 for x in pv], [x * b4 for x in pv],
+                    [x * b2 for x in pv], pv, alphabet[0:1])
+            (_DECODE_INFO_AF if autofix else _DECODE_INFO)[alphabet] = info
+    if info is not None:
+        table, b8, p6, p4, p2, pv, z = info
+        v = v.lstrip(z)
+        digits = v.translate(table)
+        if b'\xff' not in digits:
+            acc = 0
+            it = iter(memoryview(_ZPAD8[len(digits) & 7] + digits).cast('H'))
+            for p, q, r, s in zip(it, it, it, it):
+                acc = acc * b8 + (p6[p] + p4[q] + p2[r] + pv[s])
+        else:
+            acc = b58decode_int(v, alphabet=alphabet, autofix=autofix)
+    else:
+        v = v.lstrip(alphabet[0:1])
+        acc = b58decode_int(v, alphabet=alphabet, autofix=autofix)
+
+    return acc.to_bytes(origlen - len(v) + (acc.bit_length() + 7) // 8,
+                        'big')

actions.reason: The 8-digit single-multiply decode, with pre-scaled pair tables and trimmed per-call overhead, gave identical outputs but improved decode_ir only to a ratio of 0.9991, against a required 0.9900. The library's decode path appears to be a very small share of decode_ir. Most of the measured instructions go to input generation and the harness's reference encoder. Further library micro-changes are unlikely to reach the 1% bar, so I am not spending more evaluations.

journal.text:
I rewrote the decode path in base58/__init__.py (lines 247-276) to handle 8 digits per step with a single multiply. It uses pre-scaled pair tables and has less per-call overhead. I read the whole module and lineage_bench.py first.

The sandbox evaluation built cleanly, outputs were identical, and the guard passed with 1 file and 27 lines. It was still rejected for no improvement. decode_ir went from 2369521971 to 2367334632, a ratio of 0.9991 against a required 0.9900. encode_ir moved to 1.0003 and check_ir to 1.0005. I gave up without submitting a candidate.

I think the library's decode is a very small share of decode_ir. Most instructions seem to go to input generation and the harness's reference encoder, so micro-optimizing the library decode can't reach a 1% gain on this metric.

Next time I should profile what decode_ir actually counts before editing anything. I should only touch decode again if the library's share turns out large enough to matter. Otherwise I should pick a metric where the library dominates.
